articles.summary: Nueva liga oficial en el Movistar Fantasy MARCA con 300 euros en juego y Aubameyang disponible
articles.body: Lo echaba de menos el Depor y los mánager del Movistar Fantasy MARCA. Fue la gran sensación de las primeras cinco jornadas, con repóker de goles y 52 puntazos. Arrancó con un valor inicial de 4 millones y a finales de septiembre alcanzó los 34. No lo esperábamos hasta la jornada 12 o después del parón y, sin embargo, chollazo Aubameyang recibió el alta horas antes del Depor-Osasuna del pasado lunes, se sentó en el banquillo, reapareció en el minuto 69 y provocó el gol de la victoria de Nsongo. Bombazo 'Auba' en el mercado por volver antes de lo previsto y fichajazo para el nuevo concurso Super Partido Fantasy con 300 euros en premios. Tenemos 400 millones de presupuesto, todo el mercado disponible (compra-venta directa), capitán gratis para multiplicar puntuaciones y el Atlético-Barça para decidir en caso de empate a puntos. Chollos como Aubameyang (22,7 millones) nos vienen de lujo para completar un equipazo con muchos jugadores del Atlético-Barça, que cerrará la jornada 12 de LaLiga. Porque cuantos más pongamos del Super Partidazo del Metropolitano, más opciones de llevarnos cien euros de premio (300 a repartir entre los tres mejores mánager). Y es que el duelo por el liderato marcará el primer criterio de desempate. Hay que guardar la alineación antes del Sevilla-Alavés del viernes (21 h.) y nos la jugamos con 'Aurameyang' de capitán. ¡Descarga aquí el Movistar Fantasy MARCA con más novedades que nunca! Con todas las competiciones: Champions, Segunda, Liga F, Premier, Serie A, Ligue 1... ¡Más premios! ¡Y con más opciones de personalización! Síguenos en X @FantasyMARCA. articles.title: Football takes a hit as AFC postpones 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia by almost a year amid heightened tensions in Middle East
articles.summary: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup by almost a year because of the conflict in the Middle East and security concerns
articles.body: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup by almost a year because of the conflict in the Middle East and security concerns in Saudi Arabia, which is scheduled to host the tournament.A number of sports events in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following Houthi attacks on the country.In a statement on Tuesday, the AFC said it had decided to move the tournament's start date from January 7 to December 23, 2027, after consulting Saudi organisers.The Asian Cup was originally scheduled to take place from January 7 to February 5 next year. The new dates for the continental showpiece are December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028.The organising committee “approved to reschedule the flagship national team tournament in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions,” the AFC said in a statement.“Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organization and delivery of the competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.”The revised dates, December 23, 2027 to January 21, 2028, will be submitted to FIFA for approval.The decision ends months of speculation over a possible postponement. Until recently, Saudi organisers had maintained that the tournament would go ahead as scheduled.As recently as last week, Saudi officials released the kickoff times and finalised the tournament schedule, in a move aimed at assuring Asian football federations that preparations were on track. This came despite deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.Last month, organising committee spokesman Muhammed Q. Alghamdi told members at an AFC meeting in Tokyo that “daily life is ongoing in Saudi Arabia,” despite the regional hostilities.Before that meeting, AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa had indicated that the Asian Cup could be postponed by a year if required, saying “we can wait until the end of November” to make a decision.The month-long tournament was scheduled to feature 24 teams playing across eight venues in three cities: Riyadh, Jeddah and Khobar. Iran have been drawn in a group with Syria, China and Kyrgyzstan for the league stage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.standfirst: La Champions vive su cuarta jornada de liga
articles.summary: La Champions vive su cuarta jornada de liga
articles.body: La UEFA Champions League vivirá este martes 3 de noviembre una apasionante cuarta jornada de la fase liga, con una noche de grandes enfrentamientos y tres duelos de máxima exigencia para los equipos españoles. El plato fuerte de la jornada llegará con el Atlético de Madrid-Bayern de Múnich, un auténtico partidazo en el Metropolitano entre dos aspirantes a llegar lejos en la competición. Por su parte, el Barcelona recibirá al Aston Villa en el Spotify Camp Nou, mientras que el Villarreal afrontará un complicado compromiso en La Cerámica frente al vigente campeón europeo, el PSG. La jornada arrancará a las 18:45 horas con dos encuentros y continuará a partir de las 21:00 horas con siete partidos simultáneos. Entre los enfrentamientos más destacados también figuran el Manchester United-Roma y el Feyenoord-Inter, en una noche que promete emociones fuertes en toda Europa. Todos los encuentros podrán seguirse en directo en España a través de los canales de Movistar Plus+. Sigue toda la actualidad de la Champions League, el minuto a minuto de los encuentros y la mejor cobertura de la jornada en MARCA.com, y escucha las retransmisiones en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: El Everton podría indultar a Grealish tras sus dos borracheras: ¿La última oportunidad del 'Party Boy'?
articles.standfirst: El técnico David Moyes valora la situación de Jack Grealish tras su suspendión en el Everton tras dos noches de juerga
articles.summary: El técnico David Moyes valora la situación de Jack Grealish tras su suspendión en el Everton tras dos noches de juerga
articles.body: David Moyes, entrenador del Everson, afirma que Jack Grealish aún tiene posibilidades de reintegrarse al club, aunque no sabe cuándo volverá a formar parte del equipo. "¿Existe la posibilidad de que retome su sitio? Por supuesto que sí", declaró el técnico de los 'toffees' sobre Grealish, el 'Party Boy' que Guardiola no pudo reconducir. El controvertido centrocampista de 31 años, que está cedido por el Manchester United, se perdió las dos victorias del Everton contra el Newcastle la semana pasada debido a un asunto disciplinario. El diario 'The Sun' publicó que el internacional inglés salió en Londres el lunes 19 de octubre, después de acudir a los Pride of Britain Awards. Tras la ceremonia, Grealish se desplazó hasta un local de karaoke situado en Victoria, donde permaneció hasta altas horas de la madrugada junto a varios amigos. El jugador habría consumido alcohol durante la noche. A la mañana siguiente regresó al noroeste de Inglaterra y, siempre según el citado medio, acudió al entrenamiento del Everton. Sin embargo, esa misma noche volvió a salir. Grealish fue visto en un pub de Wilmslow, donde coincidió con varios amigos y compañeros de vestuario, entre ellos Jordan Pickford y Tyler Dibling. También estaba Kyle Walker, antiguo compañero suyo en el Manchester City y en la selección inglesa. El grupo se quedó viendo el partido entre el PSG y el Barcelona desde una sala privada del establecimiento. Testigos citados por The Sun aseguran que hubo consumo de alcohol durante la velada. David Moyes sólo quiso aclarar en BBC Sport que "en este momento no está disponible; tomaremos una decisión junto con el club cuando consideremos que vuelve a estar en condiciones de jugar" Al ser consultado sobre si el motivo estaba realmente relacionado con su estado físico, insistió en que "lo único que puedo decir es que, por ahora, no está disponible". "No, no puedo hacer comentarios al respecto", sentenció cuando se le preguntó sobre la "infracción de la disciplina del club". El próximo partido del Everton es en casa contra el Coventry, y Moyes no tiene claro si Grealish podrá estar disponible para dicho encuentro.

articles.title: Spanish footballer dies aged 30 a day after cardiac arrest following on-field collision with goalkeeper
articles.summary: Spanish football was plunged into mourning after Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died aged 30 on Tuesday, a day after suffering a cardiac arrest
articles.body: Spanish football was plunged into mourning after Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died aged 30 on Tuesday, a day after suffering a cardiac arrest following a collision with an opposition goalkeeper during a second-division match.De Miguel collapsed after a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during Monday's match, which was abandoned in the seventh minute of stoppage time with the scores level at 2-2. The striker was rushed to hospital after receiving treatment on the pitch, but his condition deteriorated overnight.Tenerife confirmed his death in an emotional statement."Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," the club said."There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness."The club also expressed solidarity with the striker's family and loved ones, adding: "We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome."What happened during the match?The incident occurred when De Miguel appeared set to race away on a counter-attack in search of a late winner. As a long ball dropped towards him near the halfway line, Owono rushed out of his area to clear it but struck the Tenerife forward in the chest with his knee.De Miguel initially rolled around in pain before becoming motionless, prompting medical staff to rush onto the pitch. He received treatment for more than five minutes as visibly distressed teammates watched on, with some appearing to break down in tears.According to Spanish media reports, the striker suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance.Owono was initially shown a red card for the challenge before the referee abandoned the match. De Miguel was subsequently carried off on a stretcher to a standing ovation from spectators.Football fraternity pays tributeFC Andorra offered its condolences following the news, saying: "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace."The Spanish Footballers Association (AFE) also expressed its "deepest sorrow", adding: "His loss leaves a huge void among those of us who shared his passion for football, his commitment to the footballers' community, and his work defending the rights of our fellow professionals."De Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 30 appearances, helping the club secure promotion from Spain's third division as champions. He had previously played a key role in promotions for Internacional de Madrid and CD Castellón.His family thanked everyone for their messages of support and requested "maximum respect for his privacy" during the difficult time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Se suspenden los partidos de la Copa del Rey y de la Reina por la muerte de Jesús de Miguel
articles.standfirst: Además de la presentación oficial en Almendralejo del partido de la Selección sub-21 ante Japón y la presentación de Eder Sarabia como entrenador del Espanyol
articles.summary: Además de la presentación oficial en Almendralejo del partido de la Selección sub-21 ante Japón y la presentación de Eder Sarabia como entrenador del Espanyol
articles.body: La Federación Española ha comunicado este martes la suspensión de los partidos de la Copa del Rey y de la Copa de la Reina que iban a tener lugar este martes por el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel, jugador del Tenerife. La Federación hará próximamente un comunicado para saber cuándo se juegan estos partidos. Se trata de los encuentros entre Anaitasuna y Alavés y el CD Pamplona y el Eibar. Además, también queda suspendida la presentación oficial en Almendralejo del partido de la Selección sub-21 ante Japón. Así reza el comunicado de la RFEF: Tras confirmarse el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel, jugador del CD Tenerife, y como muestra de respeto y solidaridad, la RFEF ha decretado la suspensión de los encuentros previstos para este martes, 3 de noviembre, correspondientes a la primera y tercera eliminatoria de la Copa del Rey Mapfre y Copa de la Reina Iberdrola, respectivamente. Asimismo, también queda suspendida la presentación oficial en Almendralejo del partido de la Selección sub-21 ante Japón. La RFEF informará en las próximas fechas sobre la nueva planificación de sus torneos y los horarios definitivos de los encuentros aplazados. La gran familia del fútbol español permanece unida en el dolor por esta triste pérdida y traslada todo su cariño y apoyo a los familiares, amigos y seres queridos de Jesús de Miguel, así como al conjunto tinerfeño y a toda su afición, en estos durísimos momentos.

articles.title: Los golpes, un riesgo permanente
articles.standfirst: El fútbol no es ajeno a impactos fatales desde hace 150 años: el caso del meta Gallardo con Baltazar, el más recordado. “No tuve ninguna culpa de aquel choque fortuito. Dios me ayudó”, dijo el delantero
articles.summary: El fútbol no es ajeno a impactos fatales: el caso del meta Gallardo con Baltazar, el más recordado. “No tuve ninguna culpa de aquel choque fortuito. Dios me ayudó”, dijo el delantero
articles.body: El desgraciado fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel tras el impacto contra el meta Jesús Owono, cuando el atacante tinerfeñista colisionó de forma fortuita con el guardameta visitante, en la pugna por un balón dividido, es el último de una larga lista de víctimas de la mala fortuna en un campo de fùtbol. No hay deporte exento de riesgos. Y el fútbol no es precisamente una modalidad amable con sus practicantes. A la exigencia física se suma el contacto, a veces inevitable con consecuencias terribles. El pasado año, el guardameta del Colindres cántabro, Raúl Ramírez, perdió la vida tras sufrir un golpe en la cabeza durante el partido contra el Revilla, de Tercera RFEF. El impacto le provocó una parada respiratoria en el acto de la que se recuperó, pero falleció por una nueva parada camino del centro hospitalario. El primero fue José Miguel Martínez Ferrer, ex jugador del Real Betis y del Atlético de Madrid, que falleció en 1972 a consecuencia de una insuficiencia renal... tras estar ocho años en coma por una conmoción en un partido contra el Barcelona, del que se recuperó, si bien luego se complicó durante meses con otras crisis neurológicas que alternaba jugando partidos. Aunque el caso más recordado en el fútbol español tiñó de luto al desparecido Club Deportivo Málaga. En diciembre de 1986, en un partido de Segunda división entre el Celta y el cuadro malacitano disputado en Balaídos, un choque entre el delantero del cuadro vigués, Baltazar, y el meta blanquiazul, José Antonio Gallardo, dejó malparado al portero visitante. Trasladado desde el estadio al Hospital Xeral, fue sometido a diversas pruebas que no detectaron nada más allá de una triple fisura en el parietal izquierdo. Gallardo fue trasladado a Málaga, donde le realizaron diversas exploraciones para descartar daño cerebral. Según las informaciones de la época, padecía una pequeña parálisis facial y había recuperado la memoria cuando, el 7 de enero, se desvaneció y cayó en coma. El portero malaguista falleció ocho días más tarde. La puerta 13 de La Rosaleda, ya lleva el nombre del meta desde 2017. “Fue uno de los peores momentos de mi vida, lo pasé fatal. Fue difícil aquella situación, pero Dios me consoló y me reforzó para que pudiera soportar aquello. Es muy difícil que en un choque involuntario fallezca una persona, pero ocurrió. Me quedé muy preocupado, pero seguí adelante porque no tuve ninguna culpa de aquel choque fortuito. Dios me ayudó”, aseguró Baltazar. El primero del que hay memoria en el mundo del fútbol data de 1874. William Bradshaw, portero de fútbol, chocó con Herbert Dockerty, quien venía a toda velocidad, golpeándolo con la rodilla en el estómago. Dockerty falleció al día siguiente a causa de las heridas y Bradshaw fue acusado de homicidio involuntario. El árbitro ni siquiera pitó falta y Bradshaw fue absuelto por el juez.

articles.title: Piqué, presidente del Andorra, tras la muerte de Jesús de Miguel: "Lo siento con toda mi alma"
articles.standfirst: El exfutbolista y ahora máximo mandatario del club andorrano lamenta la trágica muerte del futbolista del Tenerife
articles.summary: El exfutbolista y ahora máximo mandatario del club andorrano lamenta la trágica muerte del futbolista del Tenerife
articles.body: Gerard Piqué, presidente del Andorra, lamentó profundamente la muerte de Jesús de Miguel, jugador del Tenerife que murió a consecuencia de un duro choque este lunes. El máximo mandatario del club andorrano contestó al mensaje que puso el Tenerife en las redes sociales lamentando la triste noticia. "Lo siento con toda mi alma. Descansa en paz Jesús", escribió Piqué en la red social X. El ex jugador del Barcelona estaba presente en el Heliodoro Rodríguez, estadio que abandonó rápidamente tras producirse el fatal accidente en el terreno de juego. Su club, el Andorra, también lamentó en redes sociales la muerte del futbolista y mostró condolencias a sus familiares.

images.caption: Gerard Piqué en una imagen de archivo.

articles.title: Andrés García, en la prelista de la Selección Española
articles.standfirst: El carrilero del Getafe está en la órbita de Luis de la Fuente y podría llamarle este viernes
articles.summary: El carrilero del Getafe está en la órbita de Luis de la Fuente y podría llamarle este viernes
articles.body: La temporada de Andrés García no ha pasado desapercibida para Luis de la Fuente. El carrilero azulón es uno de los jugadores que está en la prelista del seleccionador español para la próxima convocatoria, que verá la luz este viernes. La Selección afronta en el próximo parón los duelos de la Nations League frente a la República Checa e Inglaterra y el futbolista, que está cuajando un gran año a las órdenes de José Bordalás en el Coliseum, podría ser uno de los presentes en ambos compromisos. Andrés García ha disputado este curso 14 encuentros entre LaLiga y Conference League, anotando un tanto, el que ayudó a los azulones a clasificarse para la Fase Liga contra el Partizán de Belgrado. El futbolista está siendo una de las grandes noticias del equipo azulón y una pieza diferencial en el esquema de un Bordalás que ha utilizado al futbolista de lateral, de carrilero y de interior derecho. El futbolista también fue protagonista de la victoria contra el Sevilla. Suya fue la acción en la que se pedía una falta suya que no existió y que supuso el tanto de Martín Satriano para poner el 2-1. Llegó al Aston Villa tras sobresalir en el Levante y, tras tener pocos minutos a las órdenes de Unai Emery, salió cedido al sur de la Comunidad de Madrid, donde se ha estrenado en Primera División con una nota sobresaliente.

images.caption: Andrés García durante un entrenamiento con el Getafe.

articles.title: Laporta: "Estamos consternados por la muerte de Jesús de Miguel"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Barça confirma que habrá minuto de silencio por el jugador del Tenerife y por las víctimas del accidente en Toledo
articles.summary: El presidente del Barça confirma que habrá minuto de silencio por el jugador del Tenerife y por las víctimas del accidente en Toledo
articles.body: El presidente del FC Barcelona, Joan Laporta, ha asegurado este martes que en el club azulgrana están "consternados" por el "trágico" fallecimiento del delantero del CD Tenerife Jesús de Miguel, y ha expresado su "más sincero pésame a la familia y los compañeros" del jugador. "Estamos consternados por la muerte de Jesús de Miguel, jugador del tenerife. Ha sido trágico y, como presidente del Barça y en representación del club, envío nuestro más sincero pésame a la familia, a sus compañeros, al Tenerife y a la afición del Tenerife. Ha sido muy impactante. Un recuerdo para él como deportista y para sus familiares", ha afirmado. De Miguel, de 30 años, ha fallecido este martes en el Hospital Universitario de Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria, donde estaba ingresado desde anoche en cuidados intensivos a consecuencia del fuerte golpe que sufrió durante el partido contra el Andorra. Laporta ha atendido a los medios de comunicación antes del almuerzo de directivas previo al partido que enfrentará este martes por la noche en el Spotify Camp Nou al Barcelona y al Aston Villa inglés en la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Liga de Campeones. "Hoy, en el estadio, por Jesús de Miguel y las víctimas de Toledo, se hará un minuto de silencio", dijo el presidente.

images.caption: Laporta. FC BARCELONA

articles.title: El Valencia guarda un minuto de silencio en una sesión en Mestalla, con foto oficial y comida de equipo antes de recibir al Madrid
articles.standfirst: La plantilla tuvo un gesto de respeto y condolencias en memoria de Jesús de Miguel, delantero del Tenerife fallecido tras un fuerte golpe en el pecho
articles.summary: La plantilla guardó un minuto de silencio en memoria de Jesús de Miguel, delantero del Tenerife fallecido tras un fuerte golpe en el pecho
articles.body: La plantilla del Valencia celebró este martes una comida de equipo después del entrenamiento matinal en Mestalla, una jornada poco habitual en la rutina del primer equipo y marcada también por el homenaje a Jesús de Miguel, futbolista del Tenerife fallecido este martes. Antes de iniciar la sesión de trabajo, jugadores, técnicos y empleados del club guardaron un minuto de silencio en memoria del delantero. El gesto de respeto presidió una mañana distinta a las habituales, en el centro del campo de Mestalla, con la presencia del director general, Javier Solís, y del director deportivo, Braulio Vázquez, con el resto de la plantilla y el staff del primer equipo. El entrenamiento se desarrolló en el césped de Mestalla, una circunstancia nada habitual durante la temporada. La elección del estadio respondió a motivos organizativos, ya que una vez concluida la sesión el equipo debía realizar la fotografía oficial del curso 2026-27 sobre el césped del coliseo valencianista, precisamente en la última campaña del estadio más antiguo de Primera división. Tras la sesión de trabajo, la plantilla se dirigió a pie hasta un restaurante cercano, en la avenida de Aragón para compartir una comida de grupo. Las imágenes de la llegada de jugadores y miembros del cuerpo técnico fueron captadas por Radio MARCA Valencia. La cita se produce en una semana importante para el conjunto dirigido por Javier Aguirre. El Valencia prepara la visita del Real Madrid en el último compromiso liguero antes del parón internacional y lo hace después de la victoria lograda el pasado fin de semana frente al Elche en el Martínez Valero, un triunfo que permitió al equipo recuperar confianza tras varias jornadas de resultados irregulares. El Valencia continúa en puestos de descenso a pesar del importante triunfo el domingo en un partido que quedó marcado por el regreso de Umar Sadiq tras dos meses de lesión, una reaparición fundamental por cuanto fue clave para lograr la victoria, con un tanto muy oportuno en la segunda parte.

images.caption: Minuto de silencio del Valencia en el estadio de Mestalla. VALENCIA CF
Los jugadores del Valencia se dirigen al restaurante tras el entrenamiento.

articles.title: A defensive heavyweight returns! Arsenal welcome William Saliba back as Arteta gets timely injury boost
articles.summary: Arsenal have received a massive boost ahead of the festive period with the news that William Saliba has officially returned to first-team training. The Frenc...
articles.body:
Arsenal have received a massive boost ahead of the festive period with the news that William Saliba has officially returned to first-team training. The French international, who has been sidelined since the World Cup, is now back in the fold as the Gunners look to maintain their position at the summit of the Premier League table.

Arteta is facing the kind of selection headache that most managers across Europe would dream of. After a lengthy absence due to a back injury sustained during France's World Cup campaign, Saliba is finally back in the mix. The 25-year-old was a fundamental pillar of the Arsenal side that ended a 22-year wait for a league title last season, and his recovery marks a significant milestone for the club's medical department. While the Gunners have managed exceptionally well in his absence, the reintroduction of a player who has made four consecutive PFA Team of the Year appearances is a terrifying prospect for their rivals.

Saliba's injury journey has been a delicate one, involving specialist consultations and a careful rehabilitation process that avoided the need for surgery. Having spent weeks performing individual drills, his transition back to the main group comes at a perfect time. According to BBC Sport , Saliba is part of the Arsenal travelling squad for the next UCL game against Slavia. This inclusion suggests the defender is close to competitive action, providing Arteta with elite defensive cover just as the fixture list begins to congest.

While Saliba has been watching from the sidelines, summer arrival Ezri Konsa has done more than just fill a gap; he has arguably become indispensable. Joining from Aston Villa in a deal worth £55m, the England international has transitioned seamlessly into the North London environment. Partnering Gabriel Magalhaes, Konsa has been a vital part of a backline that has surrendered only five goals in their first nine matches. This defensive solidity has allowed Arsenal to reclaim their spot at the top of the table, proving that the recruitment strategy over the summer was pinpoint in its execution.

The manager described the way the former Villa man has adapted as "unbelievable" when speaking to BBC Sport . Konsa brought a wealth of experience to London, having made 286 appearances during his time in the Midlands, which included a Europa League triumph. His physical presence and speed have quickly endeared him to the Emirates faithful, especially following a dominant performance in a historic win against Liverpool at Anfield.

The dilemma for Arteta now lies in whether to disrupt a partnership that some pundits are already labelling as the finest in world football, or to find a way to incorporate both Konsa and Saliba into the same starting eleven.

One potential solution for Arteta is moving Konsa to the right-back position, a role he is familiar with from his international duties with England. This would allow Saliba to resume his celebrated partnership with Gabriel in the heart of the defence. With Ben White and Jurrien Timber also competing for minutes on the flanks, the depth at Arsenal's disposal is currently unparalleled in the top flight. This abundance of riches ensures that the Gunners are well-equipped to fight on multiple fronts, including the Champions League and the FA Cup.

articles.title: Seahawks most to blame after getting smacked by Bears on Monday Night Football
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks had another middling performance in Week 8. Seattle got smacked around by Chicago in a 34-17 blowout loss in front of the 12s at Lumen F...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks had another middling performance in Week 8. Seattle got smacked around by Chicago in a 34-17 blowout loss in front of the 12s at Lumen Field. The Seahawks and their vaunted "Dark Side" defense were no match for Ben Johnson and the Bears. Chicago rolled to an easy victory while Seattle was left with several burning questions.

The Seahawks are now 4-4 on the season and still alive in the NFC West division race. However, Seattle cannot afford to loss any more divisional matchups, especially against LA and San Francisco. Unless something drastically changes, there's little chance that three teams from the division will all make the NFC playoffs this winter. That puts the Seahawks under a ton of pressure to diagnose their issues and to fix them ASAP.

So what exactly went wrong for Seattle in this one? And should Seahawks fans start being worried about the team's chances of getting to the playoffs?

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

These are the Seahawks most to blame for their ugly loss to the Bears on Monday Night Football.

Sam Darnold looked terrible against Chicago's defense after Jeffery Simmons addition

This version of Sam Darnold is not the same one who won a Super Bowl last season.

Darnold played poorly on Monday night, completing only 50% of his passes against a decent Chicago defense. He finished 17-of-34 for 188 passing yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Darnold was also sacked three times.

The only thing going right for Seattle's passing attack was targeting Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Seattle's superstar receiver led the team with 11 targets and turned them into six receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown. Nobody aside from JSN made a big impact on offense, be it running backs or wide receivers.

At this point, Darnold looks like an average quarterback at best over a large sample size. Kudos to him for getting hot last season and taking Seattle to the Super Bowl. But now the decision to roll with Darnold again looks pretty risky, especially with his supporting cast not being as good.

Seattle was without wide receiver Rashid Shaheed in this one. Adding just one more weapon on offense and special teams could have helped the Seahawks a lot in this game.

While Shaheed's absence needs to be factored in, it shouldn't take away from how poorly Darnold played overall.

Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price returns didn't fix the running game

Seattle finally got see their complete backfield in action against Chicago. The early returns are not very good.

The Seahawks gave the rookie Price lead back duties while sprinkling in Charbonnet in his return from injury. Neither running back found much running room throughout the entire game.

Price and Charbonnet combined for 16 carries for 52 rushing yards. The Bears had an easy time of slowing down the rushing attack, which put even more pressure on Darnold to drive the entire offense. This played right in Chicago's hand as they unleashed Jeffery Simmons in his debut game.

The silver lining is that newcomer Quenton Nelson looked pretty solid in his Seattle debut. Perhaps the run game will improve once Nelson gets settled in and Charbonnet gains a larger role in the backfield.

But will the Seahawks be able to survive long enough for their woeful rushing attack to get back on track?

Seattle couldn't count on their special teams unit either

Seattle's defense will not be mentioned here despite giving up 34 points to Chicago. That seems fair when looking at how poorly the offense played, paired with all of the Seahawks' special teams gaffes. The defense was essentially the only unit that played adequately in Week 8.

The Seahawks made multiple errors on special teams that kept the game from swinging in their favor.

Arguably the worst mistake came by safety Rodney Thomas. Nehemiah Pritchett did a fantastic job of downing a punt inside the five-yard line. Instead of leaving the ball alone, Thomas slid in and carried the ball with himself into the end zone. Chicago would have been pinned deep, likely starting at their own two-yard line. But Thomas' boneheaded mistake set the Bears up at their own 20-yard line instead, completely bailing them out.

Seattle also straight up left points on the field.

Kicker Jason Myers shanked an extra point attempt and had a short field goal blocked. Those two gaffes took four points directly off the board.

These missed opportunities did not determine the outcome of the game by themself. However, they contributed to the losing effort and showed just how unprepared the Seahawks were for primetime.

Ultimately, head coach Mike Macdonald deserves some blame too for not having his team ready to compete. One of Seattle's secret ingredients last season was the team's preparation and attention to detail. Without those edges, the Seahawks just don't look like the same team that won a Super Bowl last season.

Hopefully Seattle can turn things around after falling to 4-4 on the season.

articles.title: Tynan Thompson scores first goal for Man United as U19s drop points to AS Roma after controversial penalty
articles.summary: Manchester United U19s hosted AS Roma U19s on Tuesday afternoon at Leigh Sports Village in the UEFA Youth League.Adam Lawrence’s side have mirrored the first...
articles.body:
Manchester United U19s hosted AS Roma U19s on Tuesday afternoon at Leigh Sports Village in the UEFA Youth League.

Adam Lawrence's side have mirrored the first team's results in the competition, opening with a win before suffering two losses, although they put up much more of a fight in those fixtures.

The young Red Devils looked to bring their U18s form into the competition, having made it 10 matches unbeaten for Darren Fletcher's side after defeating Blackburn Rovers at the weekend.

It was almost a nightmare start for United when Mandjou Camara burst past Albert Mills to the byline and cut the ball across goal for Tommaso Marchetti, who, fortunately for United, had overrun the pass, which saw an easy finish go begging.

United soon found their feet, however, and took control of the match, with the Italian visitors unable to keep up with United in midfield and committing a number of late fouls in quick succession on both Jack and Tyler Fletcher.

The best chance of the opening half hour came from Jacob Watson, whose deflected shot whizzed narrowly past the left post.

United then found the back of the net shortly after when Tyler Fletcher's free kick delivery bounced into the goal untouched, but the referee disallowed the goal for an unclear reason, with no one in an offside position and minimal contact in the area.

The first half saw some lovely football from United, with quick one-touch passing opening a lane for Jaume Camacho , but the Spaniard's strike was a tame effort for Levente Kilvinger to collect.

In the 39th minute, United took the lead when Bendito Mantato beat his man on the outside and whipped in a low cross that Tynan Thompson did well to get his body over and keep on target as the ball flew through the hands of the keeper.

Moments later, Thompson was on the receiving end of an aggressive push into his neck, but the referee took no action against Giampaolo Bonifazi, and the score remained 1-0 going into the break.

Roma came out on the front foot in the second half after sitting back for much of the opening 45 minutes, but United were up to the task defensively.

Camacho almost produced a magical goal when he skipped past two defenders before nutmegging a third, but ultimately overran the ball as the keeper slid out to collect.

United could have put the match to bed when they hit on the break. Amir Ibragimov saw his effort saved before Noah Ajayi lifted the ball over the keeper, but Roma had defenders retreating to the goal line to clear.

A minute later, controversy struck when a powerful cross was bulleted off Watson's arm, which was tucked into his body, but after a loud claim from Roma, the referee pulled play back for a penalty.

The Australian-born Italian international Antonio Arena dispatched from the spot to make it 1-1, while United manager Lawrence gave the fourth official an earful about the decision.

Late chances came for Thompson and Jack Fletcher, but United were unable to restore their lead and had to settle for a point.

With four points from four matches, United currently sit just inside the qualification places but will require results in their final two matches against Sporting Clube de Portugal and RB Leipzig if they want to ensure survival.

United: Hardy; Helafu, Mills, Armer, Watson; J. Fletcher, Camacho (Rooney 85), T. Fletcher; Mantato (Ajayi 72), Ibragimov (c), Thompson (Brown 87).

Unused subs: Ford, McCormack, McEvoy, Orozco, Shah, Eze.

articles.title: Scholes compares Declan Rice to Steven Gerrard - and says Arsenal star could become “virtually unplayable”
articles.summary: Paul Scholes has said Declan Rice can be unplayable if he makes changes to his game and compared the Arsenal midfielder's running power to Steven Gerrard.Ric...
articles.body:
Paul Scholes has said Declan Rice can be unplayable if he makes changes to his game and compared the Arsenal midfielder's running power to Steven Gerrard .

Rice produced a man-of-the-match performance during Arsenal's 1-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday, with the 27-year-old instrumental in the decisive goal.

Rice's made a powerful overlapping run before assisting Kai Havertz's winner at Anfield, recording his fifth assist of the Premier League campaign. No player has assisted more goals so far this season.

Scholes was impressed with Rice's overall performance and believes the England midfielder can get even better if he simplifies his game.

The former Manchester United midfielder called on Rice to reduce his touches and use his athleticism to break teams open.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad, and The Football podcast , Scholes said Rice shares similarities with former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard.

"You'll never stay with him": Scholes urges Rice to simplify his game and unleash his running power

"What he did yesterday when he powered forward, you can't stay with that. And you see the physique, it's probably a little bit Steven Gerrard-like his physique. Both big, powerful, strong lads," Scholes said.

"If he decides to just play one and two touch and run, he'll be virtually unplayable. Almost in a Steven Gerrard type of way. I loved his goal at Bayern Munich a couple of weeks ago. That is brilliant, that's what he should be doing more of.

"You'll never stay with him, you'll never be able to live with him, and he's started to do that a little bit more. I thought it was a brilliant run yesterday and a great pass for the goal as well."

articles.title: 'I know who I am' - How fatherhood and a fresh start at Leeds helped England striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin find his joy again
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with GOAL, Dominic Calvert-Lewin opens up on his Leeds revival, the injuries that tested him and how fatherhood changed his outlook...
articles.body:
In an exclusive interview with GOAL, Dominic Calvert-Lewin opens up on his Leeds revival, the injuries that tested him and how fatherhood changed his outlook on life.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin grew up with a Muhammad Ali poster on his wall. The quote on it wasn't one of the boxer's more braggadocious sayings. It wasn't even particularly relevant to a kid. Yet Calvert-Lewin read it so often that, all these years later, he still knows it by heart.

Now, perhaps more than ever, he's been thinking about that memory.

"A man who views the world the same at 50 as he did at 20," that poster read, "has wasted 30 years of his life."

Calvert-Lewin isn't 20 anymore. He isn't 50 yet either, to be fair, but that 30th birthday is rapidly approaching. It's been 21 years since he joined the academy at Sheffield United, effectively beginning his journey as a footballer. It's been 10 years since the move to Everton and six since his first England cap. Three years ago, he became a father. Even his move to Leeds, which happened less than a year-and-a-half ago, seems so far away. Life changes, and it changes quickly. Particularly for Calvert-Lewin.

Yet through all the change, the highs and the lessons learned from the lows, Calvert-Lewin has kept scoring. This season, he's playing his best football since his Everton breakout from 2019-21. With 18 goals, he's the Premier League's most prolific Englishman since arriving at Elland Road last fall.

So what's the big secret? Why are the goals coming now more than they did a few years ago? What's changed?

Well, Calvert-Lewin has, and he's changed for the better.

"I think there's definitely strength in that," he tells GOAL , "and there's power that it's given me to know that now I know what I'm about. I know what I can do. I know who I am, and I know what I bring to the table. I think that gives me a lot of confidence when I step on the pitch…I'm a little bit more relaxed in times of hardship or difficulty. That comes from the foundation that I've got at home. I believe that's my main springboard, and I didn't have that when I was 21.

"I've got that now, and that gives me the confidence to go out and attack the world."

That part of him hasn't changed, of course. Calvert-Lewin has been attacking the world since his debut for Sheffield United 11 years ago. He's been attacking the Premier League for most of his career. Life, of course, has attacked him back: injuries, setbacks, narratives, droughts. They seem far away now, but Calvert-Lewin knows they aren't. If there's one thing he's learned in this life, it's that you can't get too comfortable in good or bad.

"Life goes in seasons," he says, "and it can sometimes be good, and sometimes there are difficult moments.

"But at the moment," he adds with a smile, "life's good."

This is a look inside the life of Calvert-Lewin, how it's changing and, more importantly, how it's changed him.

In football, it's easy to forget that the process is never really linear. Things don't always get better, and players don't either. So often, footballers peak early and spend the rest of their lives chasing that peak. The longer the chase goes, the harder it is to catch it.

For a little while, it was easy to wonder if Calvert-Lewin would return to his peak.

Between 2019 and 2021, he scored 36 goals for Everton, including 29 in the Premier League. He was just 22 when that run started. England came calling; he played at the Euros, and everything was going well. It was the start of something beautiful.

Until it wasn't. Injuries took hold, the goals dried up, and the narratives began, too. "Injury-prone" is the one that hurt most of all. His hamstring gave him nightmares in 2022-23. It made him miss 100 days during the 24-25 season, too. A broken toe, broken cheekbone, various knee and ankle issues - so much lost time. So many quiet moments that allowed the "injury-prone" label to become more than a narrative and something closer to reality.

For a while, Calvert-Lewin admits he was desperate to respond to it all. Now that he has, oddly enough, he no longer feels it's worth responding to at all.

"I think the obvious one is, when you get a couple of injuries, you get tarred with a brush, and it's very hard to shake that brush off. It's hard to shake that off yourself. There's no amount of words that can change that. The only thing that will change that is playing week in, week out, training every single day, and having consistency and robustness. Eventually, that narrative will filter away, but that's a hard one to shake off, as I found. I think people know what I'm about now.

"I think there probably were some narratives around me prior to me joining Leeds," he adds, "and I think that I've smashed them. It was my intention to break those narratives by performing well and doing my job well on the football pitch, and I believe that I've done that to a certain extent."

There's no big secret to shedding labels, but there is an easy way to do it: consistency. That's what the 29-year-old striker has found at Leeds. It was his arrival at Leeds, in many ways, that was the springboard. Leaving Everton in 2025 was a big decision, particularly given his connection to the club. It came during a period of change off the field, too, as he adjusted to fatherhood and married life. It was time, he said, to start a new journey.

Leeds and Daniel Farke will be glad he did. Since the forward's arrival, only four Premier League players have a better goal-per-game ratio than Calvert-Lewin. Over the last 15 months, he's scored 20 goals. Across his final four seasons at Everton, the ones that came after his career-best 21-goal season, he netted just 18.

"I never stopped believing that this is where I would eventually return to: playing at this level week in week out and finding this consistency," he says. "That's one thing that I always believed: through ups and downs over the last few years, I was capable of returning to being a goal-scoring center forward again.

"It sounds cliché, but, each day, it's just believing that you can return."

Through it all, the belief was simple: he was, is, and will be a goalscorer. He's proven that right a lot recently, which has gotten him thinking about the nature of goals and what they mean.

The most important goal Calvert-Lewin ever scored remains undeniable. Level with Crystal Palace late, Everton needed a hero. They were fighting against relegation and knew a win would seal their safety. Then Demarai Gray fired a free kick into the box, and Calvert-Lewin leapt through the air like Superman, heading home a goal that saved a club.

It was one of the more exciting goals in recent memory. Fans went wild. So, too, did Calvert-Lewin's teammates. But, in that moment, the striker didn't feel excitement.

"It was just relief," he says. "It wasn't even joy; it was just pure, pure relief."

At that point in his life, that was the most common emotion: relief. Goals didn't feel like a celebration; they felt like an exhale. The pressure on him was immense. Most of it came from within as he fought so desperately to return to his best level.

"There were periods, probably more so at Everton, where it was difficult," he says, "and scoring goals felt more like a relief than something that I was really enjoying. The difference in scoring goals at Leeds now is that I enjoy every moment, and I think because I've been through different periods in my career, I've learned to appreciate it more."

For Calvert-Lewin, each comeback from injury brought pressure to prove himself again, making it harder to simply enjoy the game. At Leeds, though, he says he's rediscovered that joy, and he believes it shows in the way he plays.

Take the recent goal against Manchester United, for example. It was a poacher's goal and, as it hit the back of the net, Calvert-Lewin played it cool. He walked towards the corner, did a forward roll and then let it all out. He screamed with joy as his teammates surrounded him.

"I always think to myself that I hope that never changes," Calvert-Lewin says. "I hope I still have that same feeling, that same desire, that same hunger, for as long as I can possibly play."

There is a new level of desire and hunger now, though. There are new feelings in play, too. That's the impact of fatherhood, which is something Calvert-Lewin feels every day.

Calvert-Lewin's daughter is three now, which means she's just starting to get it.

"I'd say, in the last like six months, she started to realize that daddy goes to football every day and plays there," he says with a smile from ear to ear. "She calls it 'Football Leeds', so, every day, I go to Football Leeds."

"She's been watching at the stadium," he says. "I've walked out with her, and that was a dream of mine: to walk out with my child in my arms in the Premier League. That was a special moment, and she's starting to understand it. She still doesn't understand to what level I play football, but she knows I play football all the time."

Well, not all the time. When he's not Leeds' No. 9, Calvert-Lewin has another crucial title: dad. The games and results aren't particularly significant to her. That fact has been one of the key influences on Calvert-Lewin. It's one of the things that's changed him the most.

Football demands a certain selfishness, Calvert-Lewin says. Fatherhood has helped him grow up and look beyond himself.

"I think, when you become a father, it gives you a completely new perspective that something is more important than you now. Something's more important than everything that you've been chasing. I think that gives me a lot of harmony in my life."

That harmony has made him a better man on the field. It's also, weirdly enough, made him a more complete player on it, too, because it's helped him rediscover his flow state.

'Got a little bit more quality than people think'

Given his height and style of play, Calvert-Lewin was naturally pigeonholed as one type of striker: he was a big guy up top. The truth is that he didn't really appreciate that fact - until now.

"I used to not like 'Target Man' so much when I was younger," he says, "but as I've got older, I've grown to appreciate the 'Target Man' label that I've been given. I see it as something that I am exceptionally good at. When it comes to being a Target Man, what does that require? My attributes suit that pretty well.

"I also believe that I can do a little bit more. I've got a little bit more quality than people think. I do have more."

The numbers show that. Compared to other strikers in the Premier League, Calvert-Lewin is in the 95th percentile in distance covered. He's in the 74th percentile in top speed. Yes, he leads the league in aerial duels, but he's also significantly more mobile than people give him credit for.

Still, Calvert-Lewin knows how this all works. He's a striker, which means he's measured on goals. The more he scores, the more those numbers pop and the more they justify that he is, in fact, a better player.

"There's flow state, and I can certainly relate to that," he says when asked about his current form. "It's when you come out of your head and more into your body, and just trust that your body knows what to do. I think it's a feeling that you get when you are performing well and you're not overthinking things. Things just come naturally.

"That's the grand old question: how do you tap into flow state more often so that, whether or not it's result-based, you're always there? I think I can definitely say I'm there at the moment, and I have been there since I joined Leeds and since I started scoring."

The goals have Leeds fans wondering how far things can go. Calvert-Lewin is wondering, too.

After five years away, Calvert-Lewin returned to England duty in March, coming off the bench against Uruguay. He missed out on the World Cup squad, but September brought another call-up and a chance to build on that return. After so long away, he was back representing his country. It's hard to articulate how much that meant.

"It's something I've loved and thought about so much since I was able to do it when I was 23," he says. "Then as time goes on, you realize more. I became grateful, but then I also appreciate it more. I appreciate it more this time around, representing England."

Returning to the national team remains a goal, but the truth is that Calvert-Lewin thinks less about those things than he used to. There was a time in his life when he laid everything out. Now, it's about the daily routine. The goals stay in the background, but he knows now that the way to get there isn't by doing big things, but a series of little ones.

You can count that among the lessons learned by the older, wiser Dominic Calvert-Lewin. There are plenty of them, in truth.

"There's a difference between me as a 21-year-old and a 29-year-old now," he says. "At 21, you think you've got it all figured out, and you think you know all the answers. Then you get to 29 and realize you'll never have all the answers. There's no point trying to understand too much. With experiences and things that you go through, I always try and see, particularly the tougher moments, as lessons now. What is this trying to teach me, as a man, in my career or as a father or as a husband? What can I learn from this?

"I think that's a different mindset I've got now compared to what I had when I was a little bit younger. You think maybe 'Why me? Why is this happening to me and what can I do about this?' Now, I'm a little bit more relaxed."

As Calvert-Lewin finishes his thought, the door opens. Mid-answer, he looks over and smiles.

"My daughter's just coming through the door now," he says. "She's throwing me off."

He collects himself and finishes before returning to his favorite role: dad.

"I think I'm very much, nowadays, what you see is what you get," he says. "Everything we've spoken about? That's generally me. That's how I live my life."

images.caption: Life changed when Calvert-Lewin welcomed his daughter three years ago.
The striker's game is more well-rounded than many give him credit for.
